headline: Record sales and margins drive a raised outlook
summary_short: On posted record Q1 FY2026 net sales of CHF 831.9 million, up 14.5% y/y (26.4% constant currency), with net income up 82.2% to CHF 103.3 million as gross margin expanded to 64.2%.
summary_long: Net sales rose 14.5% y/y (26.4% cc) to a record CHF 831.9M, led by Asia-Pacific (+44.4%, +61.4% cc) and Apparel (+45.1%, +57.5% cc), with both DTC and Wholesale channels strong. Gross margin expanded 430bp to 64.2% despite U.S. tariff headwinds, on full-price discipline. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 21.0% from 16.5% on margin flow-through and efficiency gains. Net income rose 82.2% to CHF 103.3M, aided by a much smaller FX loss (CHF 0.3M vs CHF 14.5M). On reiterated FY2026 constant-currency sales growth guidance of at least 23% and raised its profitability outlook: gross margin to at least 64.5% and Adjusted EBITDA margin to 19.5%-20.0%. Cash was CHF 1,020.4M, roughly flat q/q.
confidence_notes: Regeneration: force-regenerate mode was used to produce this summary (no prior ONON_US_FY2026_Q1 file existed on disk; this is a fresh compose, not an overwrite of stale data). reported_at is set to 2026-05-12 (the press release / 6-K filing date) rather than the shard's eventDate of 2026-03-31, which is the fiscal quarter-end, not the report date. All KPI values are reported in CHF (On Holding's IFRS reporting currency) despite the shard's '_usd_m'-suffixed key names — this is the shard's standing convention, not a currency conversion. The shard's 'ebitda_usd_m' KPI (CHF 159.7M) is a Yahoo-computed EBITDA figure and differs from the company's own non-IFRS 'Adjusted EBITDA' of CHF 174.3M (21.0% margin) quoted in the release — the two should not be conflated. Diluted EPS reflects Class A shares only; Class B diluted EPS was CHF 0.03 (dual-class structure).

drivers.explanation: Broad-based demand across DTC and Wholesale channels, with Asia-Pacific (+44.4%, momentum in China and South Korea) and Apparel (+45.1%) as standout growth categories.
Margin expansion to 64.2% reflected full-price discipline and disciplined operational execution, achieved despite meaningful headwinds from higher U.S. tariffs.
Release attributes profitability gains broadly to gross-margin expansion and efficiency, translated into higher leverage, while continuing to invest behind long-term growth priorities.
Company's own Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 21.0% from 16.5% as gross-margin gains and efficiency effort more than offset continued investment in growth initiatives.
Growth outpaced operating income because the foreign-exchange loss narrowed sharply to CHF 0.3M from CHF 14.5M a year earlier, per the income statement.
Management cited a strong start to 2026, a co-CEO leadership transition, and confidence in the premium strategy sustaining growth and profitability despite tariff and macro headwinds.
